column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/auto-release-verify.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS WORKFLOW IS. A PR-time verify gate. `detect` runs unconditionally and
# emits a repo-type; exactly one per-language `verify-*` job is meant to select on
# it and run its publish action with dry-run=true. Nothing is bumped, tagged,
# pushed or published here.
# WHY THE TABLE EXISTS — AND HOW THIS WORKFLOW DIFFERS FROM cargo-auto-release.
# The 2026-08-08 graphql-synthesizer silent no-publish came from
# `&& !github.event.repository.private` on a `ship` job: a green run that shipped
# nothing, with no row saying that was intended. This workflow has NO such guard
# in ANY job condition — `github.event.repository.private` appears here only
# inside `runs-on:`, where it picks the runner label (self-hosted for private
# callers, so a reusable workflow's billing does not land on the caller). Runner
# selection is not job selection, so the mandatory public/private publish rows of
# the sweep have no counterpart here: there is nothing to publish and no privacy
# branch to assert. That absence is itself the claim this header pins, so the
# next reader does not go hunting for a row that should not exist. `runs-on` is
# NOT asserted below — the linter models `if:` only.
# THE FAILURE SHAPE THAT *DOES* LIVE HERE is the same silent-green class wearing
# different clothes: the dispatcher is a fixed list of six equality tests, while
# pleme-io/actions/detect-repo-type emits ELEVEN identifiers. A repo of any of
# the five unhandled types passes this gate having verified precisely nothing,
# with a green tick and no warning — `verify-unsupported` cannot catch it,
# because that job fires on the literal string 'unknown' and a recognized-type
# repo is not unknown. Rows 7-9 pin that hole open on purpose: they assert the
# CURRENT behaviour so that closing it (adding go / caixa / ruby-gem dispatch)
# forces this table to change in the same PR, rather than the hole being
# rediscovered from another shipped-nothing incident.
# The single context path any condition here touches is
# needs.detect.outputs.repo-type, so that is the only key each case declares.
# No case supplies always()/success()/failure()/cancelled(): no condition calls
# one, and the linter derives needs-propagation from the selected set.
# ── 1-5: the five types the dispatcher actually handles. One verify job selects,
# ── the other four plus the unknown-diagnostic stay out. These are the rows that
# ── turn any future typo in an equality literal into a NOT-RUN finding.
rust-workspace
rust-single-crate
npm
python
helm
# ── 6: no recognized manifest at root. The ONLY input for which this workflow
# ── says anything out loud — verify-unsupported writes two ::warning:: lines.
unknown-warns
# ── 7: THE SILENT-GREEN ROW, and the reason 'go' is named rather than any other
# ── unhandled type: the workflow's own "Pending parity" comment lists
# ── ansible-collection / ruby-gem / github-action and OMITS go, so a Go repo's
# ── verify gate passes without verifying and without appearing on any TODO.
go-verifies-nothing
# ── 8: the second omission from that comment. caixa repos are a first-class
# ── pleme-io shape with their own publish workflows; here they fall straight
# ── through.
caixa-verifies-nothing
# ── 9: stands in for the three types the comment DOES acknowledge as pending
# ── (ansible-collection, ruby-gem, github-action). Acknowledged in prose is
# ── still a green tick over an unverified repo; asserted here so the day the
# ── gem-publish dispatch lands, this row must be rewritten rather than quietly
# ── keep passing.
ruby-gem-pending-parity
# ── 10: an EMPTY repo-type is not 'unknown'. If the detect step's output is ever
# ── unset (an empty `${{ steps.detect.outputs.repo-type }}` interpolation), the
# ── diagnostic job does NOT fire — the equality test is against the literal
# ── string 'unknown'. Pinned so nobody assumes the unknown branch is a catch-all.
empty-repo-type-is-not-unknown
